data.name: Gwan Moon High School : The Ghost Gate
data.detailed_description:
Streaming Mode

Hello, this is Studio AWE.

As it turns out, more people wanted to stream than we had expected. So, we've decided to come up with "Streaming Mode" as a way to allow you to stream, just with a couple of restrictions.

Therefore,

if you are planning to live stream or record any videos with the purpose of uploading them, you must turn "Streaming Mode" ON beforehand.


Streaming Mode can be toggled at the bottom of the "Options" screen accessible from the title screen.


Please note that you cannot change modes between "Streaming Mode" and normal mode during the course of the game, so please be careful.

The features of the "Streaming Mode" are as follows.

  • The "Streaming Mode" indicator text has been added in the lower-left corner of the dialogue window.
  • You can view all of the main episodes.
  • You cannot, however, view side episodes with the exception of "Shin Hyo Jin", "Truth".
  • You also cannot view any of the "After Stories" and "Another Story".
It would be greatly appreciated if streamers and viewers were to abide and respect this new streaming policy. I would also like to take this chance to thank all the streamers who have tolerated our embargo period.

Thank you.


Acerca do jogo

You can play the beginning of the story about 1 hour (6 chapters) in demo version.




Gwan Moon High School : The Ghost Gate
GMH is a horror visual novel with a point & click adventure game system.
It tells the horrid story of what happened overnight and a past that is related to it in modern Korea.



The high school built on the ghost gate...The spiritual energy awakens when the dark moon rises.

To see if the ghost stories of the school are true, to get their stuffs back that they left at school...High school students return to school in the middle of the night, for their own individual motives and start to panic when they encounter ghostly sightings. They are unable to find friends who went there together and also cannot leave the premises. The students then try to disclose the truth behind the ghost stories with a few clues...



  • Horror Visual Novel Game with Point & Click Adventure system.
  • The main episodes are 2 flows in parallel.
  • The side episodes for looking at characters' past.
  • Various collectibles such as After Stories of characters, Character Information and so on.
  • Play time : About 7 hours.

reviews.review:
[code]Curator page here-->[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/37670120/] DaRevieweD #74 [/url]<-- [i]New review every Sunday[/i][/code]

[b]Gwan Moon High School (GMH)[/b] has been in development for almost 6 years and is [b]Studio AWE's[/b] first pet project. Having always only talked about making one with his friends- he finally decided to go for it and it hasn't been easy; difficulty outsourcing help, lack of confidence in the process but he was dead set on completing it.

I first encountered GMH through the [b]Steam Game Festival[/b] (can't thank it enough) and being the gullible for horror & VNs, I was glued to it but torn by the translation. That's when I DM-ed the dev and BOOM(!?) here we are 8 months later~


[h1]! DISCLAIMER ![/h1]
I assisted with the localisation portion (grammar, suitability to English-speaking audience), we meticulously exchanged feedback as I didn't know much Korean. So, there goes my window to critique the translation... XD I also advised on some aspects and served as a QA staff of sorts~ 

Anyhoo, you're bound to notice the game's supernatural influence and school setting has some similarities to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/DeadeGuard98/recommended/251270/] Corpse Party[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/DeadeGuard98/recommended/691450/] Misao[/url]. It’s true, there are horror references here and there but GMH could not be any more different from th- well, there's the bell, see you after!?



[h1]"Doing Some Homework..."[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2422148567

[u]The Gist:[/u]
Follow two parties of friends and strangers, whom one way or another found themselves drawn to GMH on that fateful day. It could be due to a misplaced item, late study sesh, ghost rumor hunting and the list goes on! When the clock strikes midnight, will everything be alright?


[h1][u][+] PROS;[/u][/h1]

[h1]Struggling in & at School![/h1]
As is student life, you'll spend a lot of time reading and making the occasional toughie choices. Then, there are "search stages" where you need to point-and-click on sought for objects. Picking the wrong decision or failing to locate them in time might nab you the wrong ends! The events are lined up in chronological order with chapters branching between the two groups as the night progresses and optional "side-episodes" for added character backstory!

GMH lasts 9-10 hours, varying with your knack for reading and comprehension! But, the well-designed VN interface's thought of everything; text speed, dialogue log and generous save slots! Need I mention, there’s extra goodies too like model viewers, artwork and loads more~ Just sit back and relax~~


[h1]All-Nighter[/h1]
Something about being somewhere you're not allowed in- that just makes it excitingly terrifying! The dark, eerie vacant spaces of the school, especially the hallways... Not to forget the spectacular art, capable both in the moody, downer vibes but also the vibrant leisure times! Characters are real lookers too and wow, it's nice to have non-sexualized characters for once! The music gets the job done, with not much background tracks during the campaign and instead gets filled by just silence and ambiance and accompanying sound effects.  


[h1]Hey, Did Ya Hear? It's AWE-some~[/h1] 
You can tell a buttload of effort and revising went in the memorable story! It’ll fool you into thinking it's just mindless spookiness and “boos” one after another, but there’s emotions just bubbling vigorously as it peers into the window of human nature! Also, a respectful homage to works of horror like [b]The Ring, White Day[/b] and so on! Character personalities thankfully get balanced by each other's social strengths and weaknesses, with moments of development alluded to but remember it takes place all in one night, so hold your horses! 


[h1]Put to The Test![/h1]
SCARY: First off, I don't know about you- there were always ghost tales that supposedly took place in school; elementary, high school and even university now!! So you wonder, were they or rather are they ever true...? Told with such conviction and allure, it's just easier to take them as gospel while hoping for the best that you don't run into them~

Secondly, it also is a testament to the origin of and transmission of rumors, how they get warped, misrepresented as they get lost in translation! Was quite shocking because I had never thought about it... 

Lastly, how it's only when tragedy strikes that people's friendships, relationships face the biggest challenge of all! How well do you know the members of your clique? Can you put your trust in strangers...? That's something school doesn't teach you!!


[h1][u][-] CONS;[/u][/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2422152797

[h1]Reading Into It Way Too Much[/h1]
The thing that really screamed out was its lacking of a protagonist and descriptions other VNs would usually capitalize on to add that layer of visceral detail. Most likely intentional because the dev's not a hardcore horror fan himself!! As such, there are more out-loud thoughts than there should have been which can get awkward when alone. It is refreshing though as the game is purely character exchanges start to finish.


[h1]No Slacking Off...IDIOT!!![/h1]
GMH could be considered "too easy", like- y'know how complicated VNs can get...? Yeah, scratch that! I'm referring to the "Search" segments where 90% of the time, they're either in your face or achingly obvious, and should you arrive at a game over; the objects shimmer like diamonds! 

DISCLAIMER: I feel as though some players could be put off by the "anti-climactic", "rushed" finale or the use of MacGuffins, albeit sparingly. Personally, I liked it, as it tied up most loose ends, but if you're expecting an [spoiler] epic, otherworldly showdown that determines the fate of the world[/spoiler]. Sorry... deal with it~


[h1]Don't They Ever Learn?[/h1]
NITPICK: It's in keeping with the story but I would have loved for it to have brought its A-game when it came to the horror. It didn't go for the over-desensitized torture route that Corpse Party's guilty of, nor did it fully utilize its jump scares, just became routine.

GMH's score had only one or two songs that stuck out, which is probably why there isn’t a "music-player" unlockable. The most staying track was the main theme- which the developer wrote the lyrics and oversaw the composition! Also, the sound of footsteps and other repetitive effects did have me tone deaf and weary after 40 or so chapters, but it's something you can... well, try to get past.


[h1]"-Which Means; Going Home to Work!"[/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2422150289

GMH fits rather timely with its well-woven grounded story in a genre flooded by guts and fan service. It doesn’t make you quiver- why bother when its horror is more subliminal. Prepare to be schooled~ I can’t get over the plot; its ingenuity and subversiveness illustrated the human condition perfectly! I could embody some of the colorful casts' characteristics and not to toot my own horn- the lines turned out better than anticipated... I hope. The campaign alone is reason enough to play it, but the usual shebang of post-game unlockables doesn't detract the fun~

It was odd for a VN to not include a "main character", let alone dictate their inner thoughts or the standard descriptive poetic-waxing. Then there are other nitpicks like it not being that atmospheric, frightening (all else considered) and could be a breeze for some. But if you're jonesing for a quasi-horror fix that houses a very intriguing plot and naive students losing their cool- then GMH is the place for you~

[h1]8 / 10[/h1]


[code][i]Sincerest apologies & gratitude to [b]Studio Awe[/b], been a blast working with ya! Hope you have a good launch! FIGHTING!![/i][/code]
